- architect: Designs system architecture and module boundaries before coding (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- backtesting-verifier: Reviews backtests for lookahead bias, data leakage, survivorship bias, overfitting, and implementation realism. Use after any strategy or backtest code change before trusting the results or promoting to paper/live trading. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- cicd-safety-auditor: Reviews CI/CD pipelines for flight software and safety-critical systems. Checks build reproducibility, artifact traceability, qualified vs unqualified tool separation, and compliance with DO-178C toolchain requirements. Use before any CI/CD configuration change or toolchain update. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- cpp-cmake-specialist: Handles C++17 implementation and CMake build system for the Silmulator's simulation core. Knows the project's C++ conventions, CMake structure, Python binding patterns, and performance-sensitive areas. Use for any C++ core or build system change. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- cross-platform-checker: Catches platform-specific assumptions that work on one OS but break on another — path separators, line endings, filesystem case sensitivity, platform APIs, shell assumptions. Use before any code that will run on both Mac and Linux (or Windows/Mac/Linux). (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- dependency-auditor: Checks that declared dependencies match actual usage across requirements.txt, CMakeLists.txt, package.json, and imports. Flags undeclared dependencies, unused declared dependencies, version drift, and security vulnerabilities in the dependency graph. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- deploy-checker: Verifies that a build actually produced the expected deliverables before declaring success — DMG built, installer works, web files render, binaries execute. Catches the class of failures where the build "succeeded" but didn't produce the thing you needed. (Tools: Read, Bash, Glob)

- devops-pipeline-reviewer: Reviews automation scripts, deployment pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code for reliability, idempotency, rollback safety, and audit trail quality. Specific to flight software DevOps concerns — not generic CI/CD advice. Use before any pipeline or infra change. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- execution-auditor: Reviews order management system (OMS) code for correct handling of fills, partial fills, cancels, and edge cases around market open/close. Use before any OMS change or when connecting to a new execution venue. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- explorer: Maps unfamiliar codebases and reports findings concisely (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- game-state-auditor: Reviews NPC action handling code to ensure proposed actions cannot corrupt game state. Focuses on the trust boundary between LLM output and C++ execution, validation logic, and edge cases in the action system. Use before merging any change to NPC action handling or the dialogue schema. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- hardware-spec-researcher: Given a real device model name, finds its SCPI command set from its programming manual and formats it for implementation in Silmulator. Use before implementing a new real-device simulator to ensure the command set is accurate. (Tools: Read, Write, Glob)

- market-data-validator: Validates market data ingestion pipelines for correctness, timezone handling, corporate action adjustments, missing bar detection, and stale data protection. Use before any data pipeline change and before running backtests on new data. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- misra-reviewer: Reviews C or C++ code against MISRA C:2023 and MISRA C++:2023 guidelines. Flags Mandatory, Required, and Advisory violations, identifies deviation candidates, and prepares findings for formal deviation records. Use on any safety-critical C or C++ code before review or static analysis tool runs. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- npc-dialogue-designer: Designs and implements NPC dialogue systems for the LLM-NPC game. Knows the schema-as-contract principle, structured JSON output format, character constraint system, function-calling trust boundary, and token efficiency patterns. Use when adding a new NPC type, behavior, or modifying the dialogue schema. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- prompt-optimizer: Reviews and tightens NPC system prompts for token efficiency without losing character fidelity or schema compliance. Measures token count impact and validates that optimized prompts produce the same schema-compliant outputs. Use after any NPC prompt change and before shipping a new character. (Tools: Read, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- pyqt6-block-builder: Builds new hardware block components for the Silmulator PyQt6 drag-and-drop GUI. Knows the block pattern, canvas integration, signal/slot connections, and visual conventions. Use when adding a new device type that needs a GUI representation on the canvas. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- requirements-tracer: Checks bidirectional traceability between system requirements, HLR, LLR, code, and tests. Finds orphaned requirements, orphaned code, missing test coverage by requirement, and broken traceability chains. Core DO-178C compliance foundation. Use before any compliance review or DER interaction. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- reviewer: Reviews recent diffs for bugs, security issues, and style (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- risk-reviewer: Reviews trading code for unintended orders, runaway position sizing, missing kill switches, and dangerous execution logic. The trading equivalent of a strict-reviewer. Use before any change to order management, position sizing, execution logic, or live trading infrastructure. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scpi-implementer: Implements SCPI command handlers for new virtual devices in the Silmulator project. Knows the BaseDevice pattern, mandatory IEEE 488.2 commands, short-form aliasing, ErrorQueue behavior, and register conventions. Use when adding a new device class or extending an existing one's command set. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- software-lifecycle-doc-reviewer: Reviews DO-178C software lifecycle plans (PSAC, SDP, SVP, SCMP, SQAP) for internal consistency, completeness, and coherence with each other before DER review. Plans are where compliance breaks first — this agent catches the "plan says X but we're doing Y" gaps before they become audit findings. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- strict-reviewer: Adversarial reviewer for milestone audits, releases, and high-stakes changes. Assumes code is wrong until proven right. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- tester: Writes and runs tests for new or modified code (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash)

- tool-qualification-prep: Prepares Tool Operational Requirements (TOR), qualification evidence structure, and TQL determination for DO-330 tool qualification. Use when a development or verification tool needs to be qualified for use in a DAL A-D software project. (Tools: Read, Write, Grep, Glob)

"""Tests for the drag-to-connect wiring flow on the canvas.

Regression coverage for the bug where the in-progress "rubber" wire was
returned by ``itemAt`` in ``mouseReleaseEvent`` and silently swallowed the
click on the destination port, so blocks never connected.

PyQt6 forbids direct instantiation of ``QGraphicsSceneMouseEvent``, so we
exercise the same call path that ``mousePressEvent`` / ``mouseReleaseEvent``
use internally: ``_start_wire`` → ``_port_at`` → ``connect_ports``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import pytest
from PyQt6.QtCore import QEvent, QPointF, QLineF, Qt
from PyQt6.QtGui import QMouseEvent
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication

from silmulator.gui.canvas import CanvasScene, CanvasView, WireItem


def _simulate_drag(scene: CanvasScene, src_port, target_pos: QPointF):
    """Mirror what mousePress/Move/Release do, end-to-end."""
    scene._start_wire(src_port, src_port.scenePos())
    scene._temp_wire.setLine(QLineF(src_port.scenePos(), target_pos))
    target = scene._port_at(target_pos)
    wire = None
    if target is not None and target is not scene._connecting:
        wire = scene.connect_ports(scene._connecting, target)
    scene._cancel_wire()
    return wire


@pytest.fixture
def scene(qapp):
    return CanvasScene()


def test_port_at_skips_in_progress_temp_wire(scene):
    """The original bug: temp wire (zValue=100) shadowed the destination
    port, so itemAt returned the wire and the connection silently failed."""
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    src, dst = osc.ports[0], psu.ports[0]

    scene._start_wire(src, src.scenePos())
    scene._temp_wire.setLine(QLineF(src.scenePos(), dst.scenePos()))

    found = scene._port_at(dst.scenePos())
    assert found is dst, "temp wire should not shadow the destination port"

    scene._cancel_wire()


def test_drag_between_ports_creates_wire(scene):
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    src, dst = osc.ports[0], psu.ports[0]
    assert src.connected_to is None
    assert dst.connected_to is None

    wire = _simulate_drag(scene, src, dst.scenePos())

    assert isinstance(wire, WireItem)
    assert src.connected_to is dst
    assert dst.connected_to is src


def test_drag_to_same_block_does_not_connect(scene):
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    src, dst = osc.ports[0], osc.ports[1]

    wire = _simulate_drag(scene, src, dst.scenePos())

    assert wire is None
    assert src.connected_to is None
    assert dst.connected_to is None


def test_drag_release_on_empty_canvas_is_noop(scene):
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    src = osc.ports[0]

    wire = _simulate_drag(scene, src, QPointF(2000, 2000))

    assert wire is None
    assert src.connected_to is None
    assert [i for i in scene.items() if isinstance(i, WireItem)] == []


def test_already_connected_port_is_not_overwritten(scene):
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    fgen = scene.add_block("Function Generator", QPointF(1000, 0))
    a, b, c = osc.ports[0], psu.ports[0], fgen.ports[0]

    _simulate_drag(scene, a, b.scenePos())
    assert a.connected_to is b

    second = _simulate_drag(scene, a, c.scenePos())
    assert second is None
    assert a.connected_to is b
    assert c.connected_to is None


def test_temp_wire_is_cleaned_up_after_drag(scene):
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    _simulate_drag(scene, osc.ports[0], psu.ports[0].scenePos())

    assert scene._connecting is None
    assert scene._temp_wire is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# End-to-end drag through the real QGraphicsView event path.
#
# Regression coverage for the bug where CanvasScene's mouse handlers never
# accepted the events: the view (RubberBandDrag mode) treated the unaccepted
# press as the start of a rubber-band selection that drew over the wire drag
# and replaced the scene selection on every move.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _send_mouse(view: CanvasView, etype: QEvent.Type, scene_pos: QPointF,
                button: Qt.MouseButton, buttons: Qt.MouseButton) -> None:
    """Deliver a synthetic mouse event to the view's viewport, the same way
    a real click arrives (view → scene), in viewport coordinates."""
    viewport = view.viewport()
    view_pt = view.mapFromScene(scene_pos)
    event = QMouseEvent(
        etype, QPointF(view_pt), QPointF(viewport.mapToGlobal(view_pt)),
        button, buttons, Qt.KeyboardModifier.NoModifier,
    )
    QApplication.sendEvent(viewport, event)


def test_real_mouse_drag_connects_ports_without_rubber_band(scene):
    """Press → move → release through the view must create the wire and must
    NOT start a rubber-band selection over the drag."""
    view = CanvasView(scene)
    view.resize(1200, 600)
    view.show()

    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    src, dst = osc.ports[0], psu.ports[0]
    view.centerOn(QPointF(350, 100))

    _send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseButtonPress, src.scenePos(),
                Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
    midpoint = (src.scenePos() + dst.scenePos()) / 2
    _send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseMove, midpoint,
                Qt.MouseButton.NoButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
    _send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseMove, dst.scenePos(),
                Qt.MouseButton.NoButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)

    assert view.rubberBandRect().isNull(), (
        "view started a rubber-band selection during the wire drag — "
        "the scene did not accept the mouse press"
    )

    _send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseButtonRelease, dst.scenePos(),
                Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton, Qt.MouseButton.NoButton)

    assert src.connected_to is dst
    assert dst.connected_to is src
    assert any(isinstance(i, WireItem) for i in scene.items())
    assert scene.selectedItems() == [], (
        "a wire drag must not select blocks via rubber-band"

"""Drive the real Silmulator app: add two blocks via toolbar clicks,
drag-connect their ports with synthetic mouse events, screenshot the result."""
import sys

from PyQt6.QtCore import QEvent, QPointF, Qt
from PyQt6.QtGui import QMouseEvent
from PyQt6.QtTest import QTest
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QPushButton

from silmulator.gui.main_window import MainWindow

OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."


def pump(app, ms=150):
    QTest.qWait(ms)
    app.processEvents()


def send_mouse(view, etype, scene_pos, button, buttons):
    viewport = view.viewport()
    view_pt = view.mapFromScene(scene_pos)
    event = QMouseEvent(
        etype, QPointF(view_pt), QPointF(viewport.mapToGlobal(view_pt)),
        button, buttons, Qt.KeyboardModifier.NoModifier,
    )
    QApplication.sendEvent(viewport, event)


def main():
    app = QApplication(sys.argv)
    win = MainWindow()
    win.show()
    pump(app, 400)

    # --- Add two blocks by clicking the real toolbar buttons, like a user ---
    buttons = {b.text(): b for b in win.findChildren(QPushButton)}
    QTest.mouseClick(buttons["Oscilloscope"], Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)

content.text:
Yes and no — here's the honest picture, now that I've verified it both ways.

**Automated tests: yes.** `tests/test_canvas_connections.py` has 7 passing tests covering the drag-to-connect flow, including two past regressions (the temp wire shadowing the destination port, and the rubber-band selection fighting the wire drag). The most important one drives synthetic mouse press/move/release through the real `CanvasView` event path, so it's close to what a user does.

**Visually in the running app: I just did it, and it mostly works — but I found one real user-visible bug.** I launched the actual app, clicked the toolbar buttons to add an Oscilloscope and a Power Supply, and dragged port-to-port with synthetic mouse events. The connection succeeds visibly: both ports turn green, the orange wire draws between the blocks, the status bar updates to "Blocks: 2 Wires: 1", and the console logs `Connected [osc].CH1_IN → [psu].CH1_POS`. Screenshots are in the scratchpad (`2_connected.png`, `3_block_moved.png`).

**The bug: after dragging a connected block, the wire detaches from the port.** Wires only get repositioned inside `CanvasScene.mouseMoveEvent` (`silmulator/gui/canvas.py:232`), and they're updated *before* `super().mouseMoveEvent()` actually moves the block — then nothing refreshes them on release. So the wire endpoint permanently lags one mouse-move step behind the port. I confirmed it numerically: after a real mouse drag of the Power Supply, the wire endpoint sat at (450, −4) while the port was at (410, −20) — off by exactly the last drag step. With slow mouse movement it's a few pixels; a fast flick-and-release leaves a clearly visible gap. Notably, `BaseBlock` already sets `ItemSendsGeometryChanges` (base_block.py:98) but never overrides `itemChange` to use it — the fix is to update connected wires there (or at minimum in `mouseReleaseEvent`), which would also make programmatic moves like layout loading track correctly.

Two smaller observations: wires draw at zValue −1 as straight lines, so a wire between ports on the blocks' facing-away sides runs *underneath* both blocks and only a short segment is visible; and the in-progress rubber wire was hard to spot in the mid-drag screenshot for the same reason (it ran mostly over the oscilloscope's screen area).

Want me to fix the wire-lag bug and add a regression test for it?

Base directory for this skill: /Users/brandonlee/.claude/skills/github

# GitHub Skill

This skill covers everything needed to read from and write to GitHub
using the PyGithub library. Read it fully before writing any GitHub
code — there are non-obvious requirements (branch must exist on remote
before PR creation, label replace needs add+remove not set, etc.)
that cause failures if you don't know them.

Install if not already present:
```bash
pip install PyGithub
```

---

## Auth and Client Setup

```python
import os
import subprocess
from github import Github, GithubException

def get_github_client() -> Github:
    """
    Build an authenticated GitHub client from environment variables.

    Required env vars:
        GH_TOKEN    Personal access token with repo, read:org, gist scopes
                    (same token used by the gh CLI)

    Optional env vars:
        GITHUB_USERNAME    your GitHub login — used for assignee
        GITHUB_REPO        owner/repo string e.g. "brandon/Silmulator"
                           if not set, auto-detected from git remote
    """
    token = os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")

    if not token:
        raise EnvironmentError(
            "Missing GH_TOKEN env var.\n"
            "Add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc:\n"
            "  export GH_TOKEN='ghp_your_token_here'\n"
            "Create a token at: github.com/settings/tokens\n"
            "Required scopes: repo, read:org, gist"
        )

    return Github(token)


def get_repo(gh: Github, repo_slug: str = None):
    """
    Get a repository object. Auto-detects from git remote if not provided.

    repo_slug format: "owner/repo-name"  e.g. "brandon/Silmulator"

    Example:
        gh = get_github_client()
        repo = get_repo(gh)              # auto-detect from git remote
        repo = get_repo(gh, "brandon/Silmulator")  # explicit
    """
    if repo_slug:
        return gh.get_repo(repo_slug)

    # Auto-detect from git remote
    env_slug = os.environ.get("GITHUB_REPO")
    if env_slug:
        return gh.get_repo(env_slug)

    # Parse from git remote URL
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
        )
        url = result.stdout.strip()
        # Handle both SSH and HTTPS formats
        # git@github.com:owner/repo.git → owner/repo
        # https://github.com/owner/repo.git → owner/repo
        slug = url.replace("git@github.com:", "") \
                  .replace("https://github.com/", "") \
                  .rstrip("/") \
                  .removesuffix(".git")
        return gh.get_repo(slug)
    except Exception as e:
        raise EnvironmentError(
            f"Could not detect repo from git remote: {e}\n"
            "Set GITHUB_REPO env var: export GITHUB_REPO='owner/repo'"
        )
```

**Shell config** — add to `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`:
```bash
export GH_TOKEN="ghp_your_token_here"
export GITHUB_USERNAME="your-github-username"
export GITHUB_REPO="your-username/repo-name"   # optional — auto-detected if not set
```

**Token scopes required:** `repo`, `read:org`, `gist`
Create at: github.com/settings/tokens → Generate new token (classic)

**Enterprise GitHub:** use your enterprise URL:
```python
from github import Github
gh = Github(base_url="https://github.company.com/api/v3", auth=token)
```

---

## READING ISSUES

### Read a Single Issue

```python
def read_issue(repo, issue_number: int) -> dict:
    """
    Read full details of one issue including all comments.

    Example:
        gh = get_github_client()
        repo = get_repo(gh)
        issue = read_issue(repo, 42)
        print(issue["title"])
        print(issue["body"])
        print(issue["labels"])
    """
    issue = repo.get_issue(issue_number)

    return {
        "number":    issue.number,
        "title":     issue.title,
        "body":      issue.body or "",
        "state":     issue.state,          # "open" or "closed"
        "labels":    [l.name for l in issue.labels],
        "assignees": [a.login for a in issue.assignees],
        "created":   str(issue.created_at),
        "updated":   str(issue.updated_at),
        "comments":  [
            {
                "author": c.user.login,
                "body":   c.body,
                "created": str(c.created_at)
            }
            for c in issue.get_comments()
        ],
        "url":       issue.html_url
    }
```

### List Issues (batch read)

```python
def list_issues(repo, label: str = None,
                state: str = "open",
                limit: int = 50) -> list[dict]:
    """
    List issues, optionally filtered by label.

    Common label filters:
        "ready-for-ai"    tonight's work queue
        "ai-blocked"      needs your attention
        "needs-human"     Claude couldn't attempt these
        "ai-completed"    done, PRs open for review

    Example:
        gh = get_github_client()
        repo = get_repo(gh)

        # Tonight's queue
        issues = list_issues(repo, label="ready-for-ai")

        # Everything blocked
        issues = list_issues(repo, label="ai-blocked")

        # All open issues
        issues = list_issues(repo)

        for i in issues:
            print(i["number"], i["title"], i["labels"])
    """
    kwargs = {"state": state}
    if label:
        kwargs["labels"] = [repo.get_label(label)]

    results = repo.get_issues(**kwargs)

    output = []
    for issue in results:
        # Skip pull requests (GitHub returns PRs in issues endpoint)
        if issue.pull_request:
            continue
        output.append({
            "number":  issue.number,
            "title":   issue.title,
            "labels":  [l.name for l in issue.labels],
            "state":   issue.state,
            "url":     issue.html_url
        })
        if len(output) >= limit:
            break

    return output
```

### List Draft PRs (for morning review)

```python
def list_draft_prs(repo) -> list[dict]:
    """
    List all open draft PRs — your morning review queue.

    Example:
        prs = list_draft_prs(repo)
        for pr in prs:
            print(pr["number"], pr["title"], pr["url"])
    """
    return [
        {
            "number": pr.number,
            "title":  pr.title,
            "head":   pr.head.ref,       # branch name
            "base":   pr.base.ref,       # target branch
            "draft":  pr.draft,
            "url":    pr.html_url,
            "body":   pr.body or ""
        }
        for pr in repo.get_pulls(state="open")
        if pr.draft
    ]
```

---

## CREATING ISSUES

```python
def create_issue(repo, title: str,
                 body: str,
                 labels: list[str] = None,
                 assignees: list[str] = None) -> dict:
    """
    Create a new GitHub issue. Returns a dict with number and URL.

    body: plain markdown string — GitHub renders it natively.
    labels: must already exist in the repo. Create them first if needed.
    assignees: list of GitHub usernames (not display names).

    Example:
        gh = get_github_client()
        repo = get_repo(gh)
        username = os.environ["GITHUB_USERNAME"]

        issue = create_issue(
            repo,
            title="Add Rigol DS1054Z oscilloscope SCPI support",
            body='''## What to change
New OscilloscopeDS1054Z class in src/devices/

## Where it is
Follow pattern in src/devices/psu.py

## How to verify
pytest tests/devices/test_ds1054z.py passes.
Short forms work. *RST restores defaults.

## Constraints
IDN string: "RIGOL TECHNOLOGIES,DS1054Z,SIM000001,00.04.04"

## Branch name
`feature/issue-42-rigol-ds1054z`
''',
            labels=["ready-for-ai"],
            assignees=[username]
        )
        print(f"Created issue #{issue['number']}: {issue['url']}")
    """
    kwargs = {"title": title, "body": body}
    if labels:
        kwargs["labels"] = labels
    if assignees:
        kwargs["assignees"] = assignees

    issue = repo.create_issue(**kwargs)
    print(f"Created issue #{issue.number}: {issue.title}")
    return {"number": issue.number, "url": issue.html_url}
```

---

## MANAGING LABELS

### Create Repo Labels (one-time setup)

```python
def create_overnight_labels(repo):
    """
    Create the five overnight workflow labels in a repo.
    Safe to run multiple times — skips labels that already exist.

    Run once per repo before first overnight session.
    """
    labels = [
        ("ready-for-ai",   "0075ca", "Scoped and clear — safe for overnight AI run"),
        ("ai-in-progress", "e4e669", "Claude is currently working on this"),
        ("ai-completed",   "0e8a16", "AI finished — awaiting human review"),
        ("ai-blocked",     "d93f0b", "AI attempted but could not complete"),
        ("needs-human",    "cc317c", "Requires a human decision before work starts"),
    ]

    for name, color, description in labels:
        try:
            repo.create_label(name=name, color=color, description=description)
            print(f"Created label: {name}")
        except GithubException as e:
            if e.status == 422:   # already exists
                print(f"Label exists (skipped): {name}")
            else:
                raise
```

### Add / Remove Labels on an Issue

```python
def add_label(repo, issue_number: int, label: str):
    """Add a label to an issue without touching existing labels."""
    issue = repo.get_issue(issue_number)
    issue.add_to_labels(label)
    print(f"Added label '{label}' to #{issue_number}")


def remove_label(repo, issue_number: int, label: str):
    """Remove a label from an issue."""
    issue = repo.get_issue(issue_number)
    try:
        issue.remove_from_labels(label)
        print(f"Removed label '{label}' from #{issue_number}")
    except GithubException as e:
        if e.status == 404:
            print(f"Label '{label}' not on #{issue_number} — skipping")
        else:
            raise


def replace_label(repo, issue_number: int,
                  remove: str, add: str):
    """
    Swap one label for another — the overnight session label workflow.

    Example:
        # When Claude starts working on an issue
        replace_label(repo, 42, "ready-for-ai", "ai-in-progress")

        # When Claude completes it
        replace_label(repo, 42, "ai-in-progress", "ai-completed")

        # When Claude gets blocked
        replace_label(repo, 42, "ai-in-progress", "ai-blocked")
    """
    remove_label(repo, issue_number, remove)
    add_label(repo, issue_number, add)
```

---

## COMMENTS

```python
def add_comment(repo, issue_number: int, body: str):
    """
    Add a comment to an issue or PR (both use the same endpoint).

    Example:
        add_comment(repo, 42,
            "Starting overnight implementation. "
            "Branch: feature/issue-42-rigol-ds1054z")
    """
    issue = repo.get_issue(issue_number)
    issue.create_comment(body)
    print(f"Commented on #{issue_number}")
```

---

## CREATING DRAFT PRs

### CRITICAL: Branch Must Exist on Remote First

The branch MUST be pushed to GitHub before calling `create_pull`.
If you try to create a PR for a branch that only exists locally, you
get a 422 error: "head sha can't be blank".

```bash
# Always push the branch before creating the PR
git push origin feature/issue-42-rigol-ds1054z
```

Then create the PR:

```python
def create_draft_pr(repo, title: str, body: str,
                    head_branch: str,
                    base_branch: str = "main") -> dict:
    """
    Create a draft PR. Branch must already be pushed to remote.

    head_branch: the feature branch name e.g. "feature/issue-42-slug"
    base_branch: target branch, almost always "main"

    Example:
        pr = create_draft_pr(
            repo,
            title="fix(#42): add Rigol DS1054Z oscilloscope SCPI support",
            body=mr_description_output,
            head_branch="feature/issue-42-rigol-ds1054z"
        )
        print(f"Draft PR #{pr['number']}: {pr['url']}")
    """
    pr = repo.create_pull(
        title=title,
        body=body,
        head=head_branch,
        base=base_branch,
        draft=True             # creates as draft — human must approve to merge
    )
    print(f"Created draft PR #{pr.number}: {pr.html_url}")
    return {
        "number": pr.number,
        "url":    pr.html_url,
        "title":  pr.title
    }
```

### Close an Issue Automatically When PR Merges

Include a closing keyword in the PR body and GitHub closes the issue
automatically when the PR is merged:

```python
def make_pr_body(mr_description: str, closes_issue: int) -> str:
    """
    Append a closing reference to a PR body so the issue closes on merge.

    closing_keywords: Closes, Fixes, Resolves (case-insensitive)

    Example:
        body = make_pr_body(description_text, closes_issue=42)
        # PR body ends with: "Closes #42"
    """
    return f"{mr_description}\n\n---\nCloses #{closes_issue}"
```

---

## OVERNIGHT SESSION WORKFLOW HELPERS

These wrap the label/comment operations for the overnight session:

```python
def mark_in_progress(repo, issue_number: int, branch: str):
    """Called when Claude starts working on an issue."""
    replace_label(repo, issue_number, "ready-for-ai", "ai-in-progress")
    add_comment(repo, issue_number,
        f"Overnight session starting. Branch: `{branch}`")


def mark_completed(repo, issue_number: int,
                   pr_number: int, pr_url: str, branch: str):
    """Called when Claude opens a draft PR for the issue."""
    replace_label(repo, issue_number, "ai-in-progress", "ai-completed")
    add_comment(repo, issue_number,
        f"Implemented overnight. Draft PR: #{pr_number} ({pr_url})\n"
        f"Branch: `{branch}`\n"
        f"Awaiting your review.")


def mark_blocked(repo, issue_number: int, reason: str):
    """Called when Claude fails after 2 attempts."""
    replace_label(repo, issue_number, "ai-in-progress", "ai-blocked")
    add_comment(repo, issue_number,
        f"Blocked overnight: {reason}\n\n"
        f"Needs human review before re-queuing.")


def mark_needs_human(repo, issue_number: int, reason: str):
    """Called when an issue is too vague to attempt."""
    replace_label(repo, issue_number, "ready-for-ai", "needs-human")
    add_comment(repo, issue_number,
        f"Skipped overnight — could not attempt autonomously:\n\n"
        f"{reason}\n\n"
        f"Clarify and re-label `ready-for-ai` to re-queue.")
```

---

## COMPLETE WORKING EXAMPLE

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Example: plan and create three GitHub issues for the Silmulator,
all labelled ready-for-ai and assigned to you.
Then verify they appear in the queue.
"""
import os
from github import Github, GithubException

# (paste helper functions from above here, or import them)

def main():
    gh    = get_github_client()
    repo  = get_repo(gh)
    me    = os.environ["GITHUB_USERNAME"]

    # One-time setup — create labels if they don't exist
    create_overnight_labels(repo)

    # Create three issues for the oscilloscope epic
    issues_to_create = [
        {
            "title": "Add Rigol DS1054Z oscilloscope SCPI support",
            "body": """## What to change
New `OscilloscopeDS1054Z` class in `src/devices/`.

## Where it is
Follow the pattern in `src/devices/psu.py`.

## How to verify
`pytest tests/devices/test_ds1054z.py` passes.
Short forms work (`MEAS:VOLT:MAX?` and `MEASure:VOLTage:MAXimum?` identical).
`*RST` restores all defaults.

## Constraints
IDN string: `"RIGOL TECHNOLOGIES,DS1054Z,SIM000001,00.04.04"`
Do not modify the base oscilloscope class.

## Branch name
`feature/issue-N-rigol-ds1054z`
"""
        },
        {
            "title": "Add oscilloscope trigger subsystem (TRIG commands)",
            "body": """## What to change
Add `TRIG` subsystem commands to the DS1054Z class.

## Key commands
- `TRIG:MODE EDGE|PULS|RUNT|WIND|NEDG|SLOP|VID|PATT`
- `TRIG:EDGE:SOUR CHAN1|CHAN2|CHAN3|CHAN4|EXT|AC`
- `TRIG:EDGE:SLOP POS|NEG|RFAL`
- `TRIG:EDGE:LEV <value>` and `TRIG:EDGE:LEV?`

## How to verify
`pytest tests/devices/test_ds1054z_trigger.py` passes.
Short forms work.

## Constraints
Requires `Add Rigol DS1054Z oscilloscope SCPI support` to be merged first.

## Branch name
`feature/issue-N-ds1054z-trigger`
"""
        },
        {
            "title": "Add oscilloscope GUI block for canvas",
            "body": """## What to change
New `OscilloscopeBlock` class in `src/gui/blocks/`.

## Where it is
Follow the pattern in `src/gui/blocks/psu_block.py`.

## How to verify
Block appears in the device palette.
Drag-drop onto canvas works.
`to_dict()` / `from_dict()` round-trip produces identical state.

## Constraints
Do not modify the base block class.
Block must have input trigger port and output waveform port.

## Branch name
`feature/issue-N-oscilloscope-gui-block`
"""
        }
    ]

    created = []
    for spec in issues_to_create:
        result = create_issue(
            repo,
            title=spec["title"],
            body=spec["body"],
            labels=["ready-for-ai"],
            assignees=[me]
        )
        # Update branch name in body now that we have the issue number
        issue = repo.get_issue(result["number"])
        updated_body = spec["body"].replace(
            "feature/issue-N",
            f"feature/issue-{result['number']}"
        )
        issue.edit(body=updated_body)
        created.append(result)

    # Verify they appear in the ready-for-ai queue
    print("\nVerifying tonight's queue:")
    queue = list_issues(repo, label="ready-for-ai")
```

content.text:
Yes — every plan you gave me got a PR, and checking just now they're all merged. But the audit surfaced one gap, which I've fixed with a new PR (#25).

**The accounting:**

- **The 5 MSP430 plans from `simulator_plans.zip`** (compliance auditor, spec-driven tests, fault/drift modeling, semantic reviewer, vendor-doc generator) → all shipped in **PR #12**, merged. I verified every deliverable is present on `master` right now (`audit_msp430.py`, `msp430_faults.py`, `semantic_review.py`, the test suites, `diff_report.py`).
- **The visual regression testing epic (issues #2–#6)** → **PRs #7–#11**, all merged.
- **The connector fixes** → **PR #24** into `master`, merged.

**The gap I found:** PRs #8–#11 were *stacked* — each merged into the previous feature branch, not into the mainline. Only the bottom of the stack (#7, the conftest infrastructure) ever reached `master`. The actual payload — 11 visual tests, all the golden images, and the learning materials — was sitting stranded on the top branch of the stack, merged into nothing that leads to `master`.

**The fix:** I opened **draft PR #25** (https://github.com/bjl14710/Silmulator/pull/25) bringing those 5 stranded commits into `master`. Before opening it I merged it with current `master` in a throwaway worktree and ran everything: it merges clean, and the functional suite is green (360 passed, 16 intentional xfails). One caveat spelled out in the PR body: the 9 golden-image tests only pass on Linux — on this Mac they fail purely on font rendering (I compared the images side by side; the layouts are identical). That's by design per the epic's EC2/headless setup, but it's why I left #25 as a draft for your review rather than merging-ready.

So after you merge #25, everything you handed me will genuinely be on `master`.

# Plan: Fix Stale Connector Lines on Block Move
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: S

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Connector lines (wires between block ports) don't move when a block is
dragged — they're drawn once at wire-creation time and never recomputed
afterward. In PyQt6's Graphics View Framework this doesn't happen
automatically; a connector has to be explicitly notified and recompute its
own geometry whenever either endpoint block moves. Fix it by having blocks
notify their attached connectors on position change, and having connectors
correctly recompute their line geometry from live port positions.

## Goal
Dragging any block updates every wire attached to it in real time, with no
stale or "ghost" line segments left behind — during the drag, not just after
mouse release.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Rerouting/orthogonal wire paths — stays whatever line style is used today, just position-correct
- Performance optimization for scenes with hundreds of connectors, unless testing reveals it's actually needed
- The canvas panning bug — tracked as a separate plan

## Affected Areas
*(Paths inferred from your repo summary — confirm against the actual tree
before running `/plan-github`.)*
- `silmulator/gui/canvas.py` — block `itemChange()` override, connector registration
- `silmulator/gui/blocks/` — likely needs `itemChange()` added to a shared base block class if not already present
- Wherever the connector/wire item class is defined (likely `canvas.py` or a dedicated connections module) — needs an `updatePath()` method
- New file: `tests/test_canvas_connector_sync.py`

## Implementation Order
1. Audit the current connector implementation first: confirm lines are computed once at creation and never touched again — read the actual code before changing anything, don't assume the diagnosis without checking
2. Ensure draggable block items have `QGraphicsItem.GraphicsItemFlag.ItemSendsGeometryChanges` (or `ItemSendsScenePositionChanges`, whichever fits the current coordinate model) set
3. Override `itemChange()` on the block base class; on `QGraphicsItem.GraphicsItemChange.ItemPositionHasChanged`, iterate the block's attached connectors and call `updatePath()` on each
4. Implement/fix each connector's `updatePath()`: call `prepareGeometryChange()` first, then recompute line/path endpoints from the live `scenePos()` of both connected ports
5. Verify visually: drag a block with attached wires and confirm no ghost trails, wires track continuously during the drag

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dragging a block updates every connector line attached to it continuously during the drag, not only after mouse release
- [ ] No stale/ghost line segments remain visible after a move
- [ ] Moving either endpoint of a connection (source or destination block) correctly updates the wire
- [ ] Tests pass: `python -m pytest tests/test_canvas_connector_sync.py -v`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Block with multiple wires attached moves | All attached wires update, not just the first one found |
| Block is deleted while wires are attached | Wires are removed/cleaned up too, not left dangling with a missing endpoint |
| Two connected blocks are moved simultaneously (e.g. multi-select drag) | Wire correctly tracks both moving endpoints |

## Open Questions
- Does the current connector class already track which ports it connects, or does that need to be added as part of this fix? Confirm during the audit step (#1) before finalizing effort estimate.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `canvas: audit + document current connector position-update mechanism (or lack thereof)`
2. `canvas: block itemChange() notifies attached connectors on move`
3. `canvas: connector updatePath() correctness (prepareGeometryChange + live port positions)`

# Plan: Canvas Panning via Middle-Mouse-Drag
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: M

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Canvas panning doesn't work via mouse today and requires "fit view" just to
see the whole layout — almost certainly because `QGraphicsView`'s drag mode
isn't set to pan-on-drag, compounded by the scene's `sceneRect` likely being
computed too tightly around existing items, leaving nowhere to actually
scroll into (a documented Qt trap, not just a hunch). Fix it by wiring
middle-mouse-button-drag specifically to pan — preserving left-drag for
rubber-band multi-select — and giving the scene a generously padded,
properly maintained `sceneRect`.

## Goal
A user can middle-mouse-drag anywhere on the canvas to pan smoothly to any
area, without needing "fit view" first, while left-drag rubber-band selection
keeps working exactly as it does today.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Space+drag or left-drag panning modes — explicitly decided against, to preserve rubber-band select
- Zoom behavior changes — mouse wheel zoom, if present, is untouched by this plan
- Minimap or other navigation aids

## Affected Areas
- `silmulator/gui/canvas.py` — view/scene setup, mouse event handling, `sceneRect` configuration
- New file: `tests/test_canvas_pan.py` (pytest-qt-based, matching existing GUI test patterns)

## Implementation Order
1. Audit the current `QGraphicsView` setup first: confirm the drag-mode setting (or absence of one) and how/when `sceneRect` is computed — read the actual code before changing anything
2. Implement middle-mouse-drag panning: `QGraphicsView.DragMode.ScrollHandDrag` is bound to the left button by default, so this needs a custom `mousePressEvent`/`mouseMoveEvent`/`mouseReleaseEvent` override on middle-button events that adjusts the view's scrollbars directly (or temporarily remaps the middle-press to look like a left-press internally), rather than relying on built-in `ScrollHandDrag` alone
3. Fix `sceneRect`: pad it generously around the current items' bounding rect rather than a tight fit, and recompute it as blocks are added/removed/moved instead of leaving it fixed at scene-creation time
4. Verify: from any scrolled position, middle-mouse-drag reaches every part of the canvas smoothly, and left-drag rubber-band select is unaffected
5. Confirm "fit view" still works as a convenience action, just no longer the only way to navigate

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Middle-mouse-drag pans the canvas smoothly in all directions without needing "fit view" first
- [ ] Left-mouse-drag on empty canvas still performs rubber-band multi-select, unaffected by the pan fix
- [ ] `sceneRect` expands to accommodate blocks placed far from the origin, rather than clipping/blocking panning there
- [ ] Tests pass: `python -m pytest tests/test_canvas_pan.py -v`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| User pans far into empty space with no blocks nearby | Allowed, within a generous padded bound — not hard-blocked at a tight sceneRect edge |
| Middle-mouse-drag starts on top of a block, not empty canvas | Still pans the view; does not attempt to drag the block underneath |
| Window is resized while panned away from center | View does not snap back to fit-view automatically; panned position is preserved |

## Open Questions
- Should there be a finite outer bound on how far a user can pan into empty space (to avoid getting "lost"), or fully unbounded? Recommend a generous but finite bound proportional to current content size — confirm once the audit clarifies current `sceneRect` logic.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `canvas: audit current QGraphicsView drag-mode + sceneRect configuration`
2. `canvas: middle-mouse-button panning implementation`
3. `canvas: sceneRect padding/recompute policy so panning isn't artificially bounded`

# Plan: Canvas Panning via Middle-Mouse-Drag
Date: 2026-07-14
Status: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION
Estimated complexity: M

## The Idea (one paragraph)
Canvas panning doesn't work via mouse today and requires "fit view" just to
see the whole layout — almost certainly because `QGraphicsView`'s drag mode
isn't set to pan-on-drag, compounded by the scene's `sceneRect` likely being
computed too tightly around existing items, leaving nowhere to actually
scroll into (a documented Qt trap, not just a hunch). Fix it by wiring
middle-mouse-button-drag specifically to pan — preserving left-drag for
rubber-band multi-select — and giving the scene a generously padded,
properly maintained `sceneRect`.

## Goal
A user can middle-mouse-drag anywhere on the canvas to pan smoothly to any
area, without needing "fit view" first, while left-drag rubber-band selection
keeps working exactly as it does today.

## Out of Scope (this version)
- Space+drag or left-drag panning modes — explicitly decided against, to preserve rubber-band select
- Zoom behavior changes — mouse wheel zoom, if present, is untouched by this plan
- Minimap or other navigation aids

## Affected Areas
- `silmulator/gui/canvas.py` — view/scene setup, mouse event handling, `sceneRect` configuration
- New file: `tests/test_canvas_pan.py` (pytest-qt-based, matching existing GUI test patterns)

## Implementation Order
1. Audit the current `QGraphicsView` setup first: confirm the drag-mode setting (or absence of one) and how/when `sceneRect` is computed — read the actual code before changing anything
2. Implement middle-mouse-drag panning: `QGraphicsView.DragMode.ScrollHandDrag` is bound to the left button by default, so this needs a custom `mousePressEvent`/`mouseMoveEvent`/`mouseReleaseEvent` override on middle-button events that adjusts the view's scrollbars directly (or temporarily remaps the middle-press to look like a left-press internally), rather than relying on built-in `ScrollHandDrag` alone
3. Fix `sceneRect`: pad it generously around the current items' bounding rect rather than a tight fit, and recompute it as blocks are added/removed/moved instead of leaving it fixed at scene-creation time
4. Verify: from any scrolled position, middle-mouse-drag reaches every part of the canvas smoothly, and left-drag rubber-band select is unaffected
5. Confirm "fit view" still works as a convenience action, just no longer the only way to navigate

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Middle-mouse-drag pans the canvas smoothly in all directions without needing "fit view" first
- [ ] Left-mouse-drag on empty canvas still performs rubber-band multi-select, unaffected by the pan fix
- [ ] `sceneRect` expands to accommodate blocks placed far from the origin, rather than clipping/blocking panning there
- [ ] Tests pass: `python -m pytest tests/test_canvas_pan.py -v`

## Edge Cases and Error Handling
| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|-----------|-------------------|
| User pans far into empty space with no blocks nearby | Allowed, within a generous padded bound — not hard-blocked at a tight sceneRect edge |
| Middle-mouse-drag starts on top of a block, not empty canvas | Still pans the view; does not attempt to drag the block underneath |
| Window is resized while panned away from center | View does not snap back to fit-view automatically; panned position is preserved |

## Open Questions
- Should there be a finite outer bound on how far a user can pan into empty space (to avoid getting "lost"), or fully unbounded? Recommend a generous but finite bound proportional to current content size — confirm once the audit clarifies current `sceneRect` logic.

## Suggested GitHub Issues
1. `canvas: audit current QGraphicsView drag-mode + sceneRect configuration`
2. `canvas: middle-mouse-button panning implementation`
3. `canvas: sceneRect padding/recompute policy so panning isn't artificially bounded`

"""Base class for all draggable hardware blocks on the canvas."""

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Optional, List, Tuple
import uuid

from PyQt6.QtWidgets import (
    QGraphicsItem, QGraphicsRectItem, QGraphicsTextItem,
    QGraphicsEllipseItem, QGraphicsScene, QMenu, QInputDialog,
    QGraphicsDropShadowEffect,
)
from PyQt6.QtCore import Qt, QRectF, QPointF, QSizeF
from PyQt6.QtGui import (
    QPainter, QColor, QPen, QBrush, QFont, QPainterPath,
    QLinearGradient,
)

from silmulator.devices.base_device import BaseDevice


class ConnectionPort(QGraphicsEllipseItem):
    """A small circle on a block that represents a connection point."""

    PORT_RADIUS = 6.0
    COLOR_IDLE = QColor(100, 180, 255)
    COLOR_HOVER = QColor(255, 200, 50)
    COLOR_CONNECTED = QColor(50, 220, 100)

    def __init__(self, parent: "BaseBlock", port_id: str, label: str = "") -> None:
        r = self.PORT_RADIUS
        super().__init__(-r, -r, 2 * r, 2 * r, parent)
        self.parent_block = parent
        self.port_id = port_id
        self.label = label
        self.connected_to: Optional["ConnectionPort"] = None
        self.setAcceptHoverEvents(True)
        self.setFlag(QGraphicsItem.GraphicsItemFlag.ItemIsSelectable, False)
        self._update_color()
        self.setCursor(Qt.CursorShape.CrossCursor)

    def _update_color(self) -> None:
        color = self.COLOR_CONNECTED if self.connected_to else self.COLOR_IDLE
        self.setBrush(QBrush(color))
        self.setPen(QPen(QColor(30, 30, 30), 1.5))

    def hoverEnterEvent(self, event) -> None:
        self.setBrush(QBrush(self.COLOR_HOVER))
        super().hoverEnterEvent(event)

    def hoverLeaveEvent(self, event) -> None:
        self._update_color()
        super().hoverLeaveEvent(event)

    def connect_to(self, other: "ConnectionPort") -> None:
        self.connected_to = other
        other.connected_to = self
        self._update_color()
        other._update_color()

    def disconnect(self) -> None:
        if self.connected_to:
            self.connected_to.connected_to = None
            self.connected_to._update_color()
        self.connected_to = None
        self._update_color()


class BaseBlock(QGraphicsItem):
    """Abstract base for all hardware blocks.

    Provides:
    - Drag-and-drop movement
    - Title bar with device type and name
    - Connection ports
    - Right-click context menu
    - SCPI command routing to the underlying device
    """

    BLOCK_WIDTH = 220
    BLOCK_HEIGHT = 160
    TITLE_HEIGHT = 30
    HEADER_COLOR = QColor(60, 80, 120)
    BODY_COLOR = QColor(240, 245, 255)
    BORDER_COLOR = QColor(30, 50, 90)
    SELECTED_COLOR = QColor(255, 160, 0)

    def __init__(self, device: BaseDevice, device_type: str, parent=None) -> None:
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.device = device
        self.device_type = device_type
        self.block_id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
        self.name = f"{device_type}-{self.block_id}"
        self._ports: List[ConnectionPort] = []
        self._command_log: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []

        self.setFlag(QGraphicsItem.GraphicsItemFlag.ItemIsMovable, True)
        self.setFlag(QGraphicsItem.GraphicsItemFlag.ItemIsSelectable, True)
        self.setFlag(QGraphicsItem.GraphicsItemFlag.ItemSendsGeometryChanges, True)
        self.setAcceptHoverEvents(True)
        self.setCacheMode(QGraphicsItem.CacheMode.DeviceCoordinateCache)

        # Shadow effect
        shadow = QGraphicsDropShadowEffect()
        shadow.setBlurRadius(15)
        shadow.setOffset(4, 4)
        shadow.setColor(QColor(0, 0, 0, 80))
        self.setGraphicsEffect(shadow)

        self._setup_ports()
        self._setup_ui()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Geometry
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def boundingRect(self) -> QRectF:
        return QRectF(0, 0, self.BLOCK_WIDTH, self.BLOCK_HEIGHT)

    def shape(self) -> QPainterPath:
        path = QPainterPath()
        path.addRoundedRect(self.boundingRect(), 8, 8)
        return path

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Painting
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def paint(self, painter: QPainter, option, widget=None) -> None:
        rect = self.boundingRect()

        # Body gradient
        gradient = QLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, rect.height())
        gradient.setColorAt(0.0, self.BODY_COLOR)
        gradient.setColorAt(1.0, self.BODY_COLOR.darker(110))
        painter.setBrush(QBrush(gradient))

        # Border (highlighted when selected)
        border_color = self.SELECTED_COLOR if self.isSelected() else self.BORDER_COLOR
        painter.setPen(QPen(border_color, 2.0 if self.isSelected() else 1.5))
        painter.drawRoundedRect(rect, 8, 8)

        # Title bar
        title_rect = QRectF(0, 0, rect.width(), self.TITLE_HEIGHT)
        header_gradient = QLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, self.TITLE_HEIGHT)
        header_gradient.setColorAt(0, self.HEADER_COLOR.lighter(120))
        header_gradient.setColorAt(1, self.HEADER_COLOR)
        painter.setBrush(QBrush(header_gradient))
        painter.setPen(Qt.PenStyle.NoPen)
        path = QPainterPath()
        path.addRoundedRect(title_rect, 8, 8)
        # Square off bottom corners
        path.addRect(QRectF(0, self.TITLE_HEIGHT / 2, rect.width(), self.TITLE_HEIGHT / 2))
        painter.drawPath(path)

        # Title text
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor(255, 255, 255)))
        font = QFont("Consolas", 9, QFont.Weight.Bold)
        painter.setFont(font)
        painter.drawText(

"""Tests that connector wires stay glued to block ports when blocks move.

Regression coverage for the bug where wires were drawn once at creation
(and refreshed only during wire-drawing gestures), so dragging a block —
or moving it programmatically with setPos() — left stale wire geometry
behind: the line stayed at the block's old position.

The fix routes ItemPositionHasChanged from BaseBlock.itemChange to
CanvasScene.update_wires_for_block, so wires track continuously during a
drag, not just after release.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import pytest
from PyQt6.QtCore import QEvent, QPointF, Qt
from PyQt6.QtGui import QMouseEvent
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication

from silmulator.gui.canvas import CanvasScene, CanvasView, WireItem


@pytest.fixture
def scene(qapp):
    return CanvasScene()


def _wire_endpoints(wire: WireItem) -> tuple:
    return wire.line().p1(), wire.line().p2()


def _assert_wire_on_ports(wire: WireItem) -> None:
    """The wire's line must sit exactly on its ports' live scene positions."""
    p1, p2 = _wire_endpoints(wire)
    assert p1 == wire.src_port.scenePos(), (
        f"wire start {p1} detached from src port {wire.src_port.scenePos()}"
    )
    assert p2 == wire.dst_port.scenePos(), (
        f"wire end {p2} detached from dst port {wire.dst_port.scenePos()}"
    )


def _connect(scene: CanvasScene, src_block, dst_block,
             src_idx: int = 0, dst_idx: int = 0) -> WireItem:
    wire = scene.connect_ports(src_block.ports[src_idx], dst_block.ports[dst_idx])
    assert isinstance(wire, WireItem)
    return wire


def test_setpos_moves_wire_with_source_block(scene):
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    wire = _connect(scene, osc, psu)

    osc.setPos(QPointF(-200, 300))

    _assert_wire_on_ports(wire)


def test_setpos_moves_wire_with_destination_block(scene):
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    wire = _connect(scene, osc, psu)

    psu.setPos(QPointF(900, -150))

    _assert_wire_on_ports(wire)


def test_all_wires_on_a_block_update_not_just_first(scene):
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    fgen = scene.add_block("Function Generator", QPointF(0, 500))
    wire_a = _connect(scene, osc, psu, src_idx=0)
    wire_b = _connect(scene, osc, fgen, src_idx=1)

    osc.setPos(QPointF(250, 250))

    _assert_wire_on_ports(wire_a)
    _assert_wire_on_ports(wire_b)


def test_both_endpoint_blocks_moved_together(scene):
    """Multi-select drag equivalent: both endpoints move, wire tracks both."""
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    wire = _connect(scene, osc, psu)

    osc.setPos(osc.pos() + QPointF(120, 80))
    psu.setPos(psu.pos() + QPointF(120, 80))

    _assert_wire_on_ports(wire)


def test_delete_block_via_context_menu_action_removes_wires(scene):
    """BaseBlock._delete_block must clean up wires and registries, not
    leave a dangling wire pointing at a removed block."""
    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    _connect(scene, osc, psu)

    osc._delete_block()

    assert osc.block_id not in [b.block_id for b in scene.blocks]
    assert scene._wires == {}
    assert not any(isinstance(i, WireItem) for i in scene.items())
    assert psu.ports[0].connected_to is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Real mouse-drag path through the view: the wire must track the block
# continuously DURING the drag and sit exactly on the port after release.
# The pre-fix behavior updated wires before the block moved (one move-event
# lag) and never on release, leaving the wire detached by the last step.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _send_mouse(view: CanvasView, etype: QEvent.Type, scene_pos: QPointF,
                button: Qt.MouseButton, buttons: Qt.MouseButton) -> None:
    """Deliver a synthetic mouse event to the view's viewport, the same way
    a real click arrives (view → scene), in viewport coordinates."""
    viewport = view.viewport()
    view_pt = view.mapFromScene(scene_pos)
    event = QMouseEvent(
        etype, QPointF(view_pt), QPointF(viewport.mapToGlobal(view_pt)),
        button, buttons, Qt.KeyboardModifier.NoModifier,
    )
    QApplication.sendEvent(viewport, event)


def test_mouse_drag_keeps_wire_on_port_during_and_after_drag(scene, qapp):
    view = CanvasView(scene)
    view.resize(1200, 800)
    view.show()

    osc = scene.add_block("Oscilloscope", QPointF(0, 0))
    psu = scene.add_block("Power Supply", QPointF(500, 0))
    wire = _connect(scene, osc, psu)
    view.centerOn(QPointF(350, 100))

    # Grab the PSU by its title bar (away from any port).
    grab = psu.scenePos() + QPointF(psu.BLOCK_WIDTH / 2, 8)
    _send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseButtonPress, grab,
                Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)

    for step in range(1, 5):
        _send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseMove,
                    grab + QPointF(30 * step, 20 * step),
                    Qt.MouseButton.NoButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
        # Continuous tracking: after every intermediate move event the
        # wire must already sit on the port — not one event behind.
        _assert_wire_on_ports(wire)

    _send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseButtonRelease, grab + QPointF(120, 80),
                Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton, Qt.MouseButton.NoButton)

    assert psu.pos() != QPointF(500, 0), "drag did not move the block"
    _assert_wire_on_ports(wire)
    view.close()

"""Drive the real Silmulator app: add two blocks via toolbar clicks,
drag-connect their ports, then mouse-drag a block and check the wire
tracks it exactly. Screenshots saved to the output dir."""
import sys

from PyQt6.QtCore import QEvent, QPointF, Qt
from PyQt6.QtGui import QMouseEvent
from PyQt6.QtTest import QTest
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QPushButton

from silmulator.gui.main_window import MainWindow

OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."


def pump(app, ms=120):
    QTest.qWait(ms)
    app.processEvents()


def send_mouse(view, etype, scene_pos, button, buttons):
    viewport = view.viewport()
    view_pt = view.mapFromScene(scene_pos)
    event = QMouseEvent(
        etype, QPointF(view_pt), QPointF(viewport.mapToGlobal(view_pt)),
        button, buttons, Qt.KeyboardModifier.NoModifier,
    )
    QApplication.sendEvent(viewport, event)


def main():
    app = QApplication(sys.argv)
    win = MainWindow()
    win.show()
    pump(app, 400)

    buttons = {b.text(): b for b in win.findChildren(QPushButton)}
    QTest.mouseClick(buttons["Oscilloscope"], Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
    pump(app)
    QTest.mouseClick(buttons["Power Supply"], Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
    pump(app)
    blocks = win.canvas.blocks
    win.canvas_view.fit_all()
    pump(app)

    src, dst = blocks[0].ports[0], blocks[1].ports[0]
    view = win.canvas_view

    send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseButtonPress, src.scenePos(),
               Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
    pump(app)
    send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseMove, dst.scenePos(),
               Qt.MouseButton.NoButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
    pump(app)
    send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseButtonRelease, dst.scenePos(),
               Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton, Qt.MouseButton.NoButton)
    pump(app)
    print(f"connected: {src.connected_to is dst}")

    # Drag the PSU by its title bar with real mouse events.
    psu = blocks[1]
    grab_pt = psu.scenePos() + QPointF(psu.boundingRect().width() / 2, 8)
    send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseButtonPress, grab_pt,
               Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
    pump(app)
    for step in range(1, 6):
        send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseMove,
                   grab_pt + QPointF(-40 * step, -16 * step),
                   Qt.MouseButton.NoButton, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)
        pump(app, 40)
    send_mouse(view, QEvent.Type.MouseButtonRelease,
               grab_pt + QPointF(-200, -80),
               Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton, Qt.MouseButton.NoButton)
    pump(app, 250)
    win.grab().save(f"{OUT}/after_block_drag.png")

    wire = next(iter(win.canvas._wires.values()))
    gap_p2 = wire.line().p2() - wire.dst_port.scenePos()
    gap_p1 = wire.line().p1() - wire.src_port.scenePos()
    print(f"wire p1 gap: ({gap_p1.x():.2f}, {gap_p1.y():.2f})")
    print(f"wire p2 gap: ({gap_p2.x():.2f}, {gap_p2.y():.2f})")
    win.close()
    print("OK")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Look for: bugs (especially Qt lifecycle issues — itemChange firing before the block is added to the scene or during scene.clear(), re-entrancy, blocks whose scene is None), performance concerns in the O(wires) scan per move event, API misuse (ItemSendsGeometryChanges vs ItemSendsScenePositionChanges), test gaps, and style/convention mismatches with the surrounding code. content.text:
I reviewed the diff on `fix/wire-sync-on-block-move` (`git -C .../Silmulator diff` / `status`), read the full `base_block.py`, `canvas.py`, and the new test file, and ran the suite (`364 passed, 16 xfailed`, matching the stated baseline; the 6 new tests pass individually too).

## Verified as correct (no issue)
- `ItemSendsGeometryChanges` (base_block.py:98, pre-existing) is the right flag for `itemChange(ItemPositionHasChanged)` to fire — `ItemSendsScenePositionChanges` isn't needed since `BaseBlock` has no parent item. No API misuse.
- Lifecycle safety: `add_block` (canvas.py:112-113) and `from_dict` (canvas.py:358) both call `block.setPos(...)` *before* `self.addItem(block)`, so the very first `ItemPositionHasChanged` for a new block fires while `self.scene()` is `None`. The `getattr(scene, "update_wires_for_block", None)` guard in `itemChange` (base_block.py:131-134) is load-bearing here, not dead defensive code — it's exercised by nearly every existing test.
- No re-entrancy: `wire.update_position()` only touches `QGraphicsLineItem.setLine()`/`port.scenePos()`, neither of which re-enters `BaseBlock.itemChange`.
- Ordering in `remove_block` (canvas.py:153-164): `self._blocks.pop(...)` happens before `self.removeItem(block)`, so the block is already out of the registry before any Qt-internal notification during removal.
- No other `removeItem(block)` call sites bypass `remove_block` (checked `main_window.py`, `canvas.py`) — the fix is applied consistently across the codebase.
- No security issues (no user input/secrets/injection surface in this diff).

## HIGH
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/silmulator/Silmulator/Silmulator/silmulator/gui/blocks/base_block.py:291-292` — the fallback branch `scene.removeItem(self)` in `_delete_block` (used when `scene` lacks `remove_block`) is untested. Add a test with a bare `QGraphicsScene` (no `remove_block` attr) to confirm it still removes the item without raising.
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/silmulator/Silmulator/Silmulator/silmulator/gui/blocks/base_block.py:131-134` — the "no scene yet" / "scene without `update_wires_for_block`" guards in `itemChange` are only incidentally exercised (via `add_block`'s setPos-before-addItem ordering), never directly asserted. Since this is precisely the Qt lifecycle landmine the fix targets, add an explicit regression test that constructs a block and calls `.setPos()` before it's ever added to a scene (and/or with a plain `QGraphicsScene`), asserting no exception.

## MEDIUM
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/silmulator/Silmulator/Silmulator/silmulator/gui/canvas.py:155-159` vs `:221-224` — the predicate `wire.src_port.parent_block is block or wire.dst_port.parent_block is block` is duplicated verbatim in `remove_block` and `update_wires_for_block`. Extract a small helper (e.g. `_wires_touching(block)`) so the two can't drift apart on a future edit.
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/silmulator/Silmulator/Silmulator/silmulator/gui/canvas.py:214-224` — `update_wires_for_block` does an O(total wires) scan on every `ItemPositionHasChanged`, which fires per mouse-move sample during a drag, not just once. For scenes with many wires this is O(W) per pixel of drag. Since `_wires` mutation is centralized in `connect_ports`/`_remove_wire`, maintaining a `block_id -> [WireItem]` adjacency map would make this O(degree). Not urgent at current scale (full suite still runs in ~1.7s), but worth a TODO/comment if wire counts are expected to grow.

## LOW
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/silmulator/Silmulator/Silmulator/silmulator/gui/blocks/base_block.py:124` — `itemChange`'s `value` param and return type are unannotated, unlike sibling overrides in the same file that at least annotate `-> None`. Minor inconsistency with the "use type hints" project rule; PyQt6 stubs type it as `(change: GraphicsItemChange, value: Any) -> Any`.
- `/Users/brandonlee/development/repos/products/silmulator/Silmulator/Silmulator/silmulator/gui/blocks/base_block.py:132` and `:288` — both use `getattr(scene, "...", None)` duck-typing instead of `isinstance(scene, CanvasScene)`, almost certainly to avoid a circular import (`canvas.py` already imports `base_block.py`). It works and is internally consistent between the two call sites, but a one-line comment stating that rationale would stop a future reader from "cleaning it up" into an isinstance check that reintroduces the circular import.
